To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the genomic response in striatum is dose- and time-dependent and that behavioral tolerance to cocaine is associated with decreased preprodynorphiin mRNA.
the preprodynphin genomic response to cocaine is differentially regulated in the dorsal and ventral striatum and exhibits tolerance to chronic cocaine.

(1) the preprodynamorphin, but no preproenkepbalin, mRNA response in striatum is tolerant to chronic cocaine binges, and (2) the zif/268, but no c-fos, mRNA response in the striatum is not tolerant to chronic cocaine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of drug tolerance and sensitization.
the regulation of the opioid peptide system in response to chronic cocaine exposure.
the regulation of the dynorphin system in the striatum and the relationship of this regulation to the development of tolerance to the behavioral effects of cocaine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genomic response in the dorsal striatal region of cocaine binge-treated rats is differentially regulated by dose and duration of cocaine exposure.
cocaine-induced increases in preprodynphin and zif/ 268 mRNAs are not directly related and are not directly involved with cocaine-induced behaviors.
the genomic response to cocaine binges depends upon the dose and duration of cocaine treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chronic cocaine binges differentially affect striatal gene expression and that the preprodynrophin genomic response exhibits behavioral tolerance to chronic high, but not low, dose cocaine binges.
the preprodynrophin gene is more sensitive to cocaine than the preproenkepalin gene.
the striatal preprodysorphin mRNA response to cocaine binges is dose- and time-dependent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cocaine binges differentially affect preprodynorphins, c-fos mRNAs and zif/168 mRNAs.
the preprodynophin genomic response exhibits a differential tolerance to chronic high and low dose cocaine binges.
the genomic response to repeated cocaine exposure is dose-dependent and that tolerance develops with repeated high dose exposure.
